observed_discontinuity: FrozenBubble.onCreate pc 11 invokes Activity.getIntent(). The game VM had no method, so the invoke was skipped and the following null check treated the result as null. The same run still reached the game thread and PenguinSprite.paint, so the missing call is the first unresolved public invoke directly observed on execution context 0 and not a proven blocker.
required_semantics: Activity.getIntent returns the current mIntent reference.
The returned object is the same Intent identity stored on the Activity.
A repeated call returns that same identity.
When mIntent is null, getIntent returns null and does not allocate an Intent.
The getter does not modify the Intent, the Activity, or the launch lifecycle.

differences.description: Activity.getIntent was unresolved, so FrozenBubble.onCreate did not receive the launch Intent already stored in _intent.
differences.relevance: The call is the Activity launch-state accessor. Skipping it made the following getExtras check see a null Intent. It did not stop later painting.

earliest_evidenced_divergence: API19 Activity.getIntent returns the current mIntent identity. AGR skipped the invoke.

evidence.artifact: android-4.4.4_r2 Activity.java public Intent getIntent() returns mIntent. setIntent assigns mIntent and is not part of this encounter.

Linux get-intent-host PASS. After start, Activity _intent is the launch Intent. getIntent returns that object. A second call returns the same object and does not allocate. Replacing _intent with a distinct Intent B makes getIntent return B while the original launch Intent stays in place. Clearing _intent makes getIntent return null without allocating. The window identity and feature state stay unchanged.
